title: What is veganism?
text: Veganism is the principle that animals are not ours to use. It rejects the idea that animals exist for human purposes, as property, resources or commodities, and recognises them as someone, not something. It was defined in 1951 as the doctrine that man should live without exploiting animals. It was never a diet, an environmental strategy or a health programme, and not a campaign for less suffering. Because it rests on a principle, it needs no list of permitted and forbidden things. Think of any principle you already hold. If what belongs to other people is not yours to take, you do not carry an inventory of every object you must not steal. When a situation arises, you apply the principle. It is the same with veganism. Practices may change as circumstances do. The principle does not.
